newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Ericsson leads firming New York ADRs.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Ericsson leads firming New York ADRs.

text.p: Shares in foreign companies rose along with the rest of the New York market on Friday, with Sweden's LM Ericsson Telephone Corp leading the pack on an upgrade from Goldman Sachs.
American Depositary Receipts for Latin American companies were also helped by a stronger Mexican market, which in turn was bolstered by a stronger peso and traders' short-covering.

"There is nothing stock-specific. It's all Dow related," one trader said. He noted the Dow industrials had edged higher despite steady selling in Philip Morris Cos Inc on new information about the link between cancer and tobacco.

Among Mexican stocks, Telefonos de Mexico rose 1/4 to 31-5/8. Grupo Televisa rose 3/4 to 27-1/4 after Unilever NV said a publicity deal with TV Azteca did not represent a break in its long-running relationship with Televisa.
Brazil's state telecommunications company Telebras SA was up 3/4 to 80-3/4. "Telebras finally has made a bit of a move before the expiration of options on Monday," a trader said.

Ericsson rose one to 28-3/4, helped by Goldman Sachs' decision to upgrade the telecommunications company to its priority list from market outperformer. Its volume of 3.59 million shares by early afternoon led ADR stocks.

Another European standout was Hanson Plc which was unchanged at 6-3/4. British Gas Plc was off 1/8 to 30-3/8 and the dip followed news the company was studying whether to move ahead its planned splitup.
The 441 ADR stocks saw 160 advancers and 116 decliners by mid-afternoon. Volume was 37.6 million shares.
